_comment: Values that occupy MERCHANT_NAME without naming a counterparty. These describe the movement of money inside the bank, not who it went to, so they are not merchants and must not enter the merchant master -- doing so would put 41293 rows of settlement and transfer traffic into merchant-level totals. Separated from the employers that look similar (INDEVCO, MUREX, AUB PAYROLL) by PROCESSING_TYPE rather than by spelling: every row here is SETTLEMENT_CREDIT or TRANSFER_*, with zero purchases, while the employers are SALARY_CREDIT and are real counterparties.
_labels_comment: Kind -> the name written into MERCHANT_NAME_CLEANED. The kind token is an identifier and reads like one: STANDING_ORDER is not a name a reader should meet on a sheet beside CARREFOUR. The label is the movement spelled the way the source spells it, in words, so the column holds one kind of thing throughout -- a name -- and the words are separated rather than run together. TRANSFER is labelled INTERNAL TRANSFER because that is what it is: money between the customer's own accounts, and the bare word would read as a transfer to somebody else.
